question: In @Configuration(proxyBeanMethods = false), what happens when beanA() calls beanB() directly?
options: The container's singleton beanB is returned via CGLIB
Startup fails because inter-bean calls are forbidden
A new instance is created by a plain Java call, not the container's singleton
beanB becomes prototype-scoped automatically
explanation: Without CGLIB proxying, @Bean methods are ordinary methods, so inter-bean calls bypass the container.

question: A singleton bean receives a prototype bean through its constructor. What does it get each time it uses that field?
options: A fresh prototype instance on every method call
A proxy that creates a new instance per call by default
null after the first use
The same prototype instance, created once at injection time
explanation: Injection happens once; use ObjectProvider, @Lookup or a scoped proxy to get a new prototype each time.

question: In what order are these initialization callbacks invoked for a bean?
options: @PostConstruct, then afterPropertiesSet(), then the custom init method
afterPropertiesSet(), then @PostConstruct, then the custom init method
Custom init method, then @PostConstruct, then afterPropertiesSet()
@PostConstruct, then the custom init method, then afterPropertiesSet()
explanation: Annotation callbacks run first, then InitializingBean, then the init method declared on the bean definition.

question: Why is a @PreDestroy method on a prototype-scoped bean never called by the container?
options: Prototype beans are destroyed only on JVM exit
The container does not manage prototype beans after handing them out
@PreDestroy is supported only on @Configuration classes
Prototype beans are always wrapped in proxies that swallow callbacks
explanation: Spring configures and returns prototypes but does not track them, so the client is responsible for cleanup.

question: Why is @ConditionalOnMissingBean reliable in auto-configurations but risky in ordinary user @Configuration classes?
options: It is evaluated lazily at first injection only in auto-configurations
User configuration classes ignore all conditions
It is evaluated against beans registered so far, and auto-configurations are processed after user configuration
Auto-configurations are processed in a separate child context
explanation: Condition evaluation depends on registration order; auto-configurations run after user beans are defined, so they see them.

question: What does @AutoConfiguration(after = DataSourceAutoConfiguration.class) control?
options: That it is only applied when DataSourceAutoConfiguration is excluded
That its beans are created after the application has started
That DataSourceAutoConfiguration is disabled
That this auto-configuration is processed after DataSourceAutoConfiguration
explanation: Ordering ensures conditions like @ConditionalOnBean(DataSource.class) can see beans from the referenced auto-configuration.

question: A bean has @ConditionalOnProperty(name = "feature.cache.enabled", havingValue = "true") with matchIfMissing left at its default. The property is absent. What happens?
options: The condition does not match and the bean is not created
The bean is created because missing properties default to true
Startup fails with a missing property error
The bean is created lazily on first use
explanation: matchIfMissing defaults to false, so an absent property means the condition fails.

question: Which Spring Boot utility is designed for testing an auto-configuration's conditions without starting the full application?
options: SpringApplicationBuilder
ApplicationContextRunner
MockMvcBuilders
AnnotationConfigWebApplicationContext
explanation: ApplicationContextRunner lets you add configurations and properties and assert on the resulting context quickly.

question: How does a servlet Filter differ from a Spring MVC HandlerInterceptor?
options: A Filter runs only after the response is committed
An interceptor can modify requests before any Filter runs
A Filter runs in the servlet container before DispatcherServlet, while an interceptor runs around the chosen handler
They are identical, just registered differently
explanation: Interceptors have access to the resolved handler method; filters work at the raw servlet level.

question: In Spring Framework 6, does a request to /users/ match a handler mapped to /users by default?
options: Yes, trailing slashes are always ignored
Only for GET requests
Only when the handler uses @RestController
No, trailing slash matching is disabled by default
explanation: Spring 6 deprecated trailing slash matching and turned it off by default.

question: With Spring Boot's auto-configured ObjectMapper, what happens when a JSON request body contains an unknown property?
options: The property is ignored and deserialization succeeds
Deserialization fails with UnrecognizedPropertyException
The request is rejected with 415
The unknown property is stored in a map automatically
explanation: Boot's Jackson configuration disables DeserializationFeature.FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES.

question: What does spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true do for a Spring MVC app on Java 21?
options: It switches the app to reactive WebFlux
The embedded server handles requests on virtual threads
It enables a fixed pool of 200 platform threads
It makes all controller methods asynchronous futures
explanation: Since Boot 3.2 this property configures Tomcat or Jetty and task executors to use virtual threads.

question: With spring.jpa.open-in-view=false, what typically causes a LazyInitializationException?
options: Calling save() inside a transaction
Using @Id with a UUID type
Accessing a lazy association after the persistence context has closed, e.g. in the controller
Defining two repositories for the same entity
explanation: Lazy proxies need an open persistence context; outside the transaction they cannot load data.

question: What happens when SimpleJpaRepository.save() is called with a detached entity that has an existing id?
options: It calls persist and attaches the passed object
It throws EntityExistsException
It updates the row but returns null
It calls EntityManager.merge and returns a managed copy, leaving the passed object detached
explanation: For non-new entities save() delegates to merge, so you should use the returned instance.

question: What does Spring Boot use for spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto by default with an embedded database and no schema migration tool?
options: create-drop
update
validate
none
explanation: Boot defaults to create-drop for embedded databases when no Flyway or Liquibase is detected, otherwise none.

question: Which JPA association is fetched EAGER by default?
options: @OneToMany
@ManyToOne
@ManyToMany
@ElementCollection
explanation: To-one associations default to EAGER, while to-many associations default to LAZY.

question: An app defines two SecurityFilterChain beans. How does Spring Security pick which one handles a request?
options: Both chains run in sequence for every request
The chain declared last in the class always wins
The first chain, by @Order, whose securityMatcher matches the request
It merges the chains into one
explanation: FilterChainProxy uses the first matching chain, so specific matchers need higher precedence than catch-all chains.

question: Why can an @Async method lose the authenticated user from SecurityContextHolder?
options: @Async clears the HTTP session
Security contexts expire after one second
Async methods run as an anonymous system user by design
The default strategy is ThreadLocal, so the new thread has no context unless it is propagated
explanation: Use DelegatingSecurityContextExecutor or a propagating strategy to carry the context to other threads.

question: In Spring Security 6, a custom login endpoint sets SecurityContextHolder but the user is unauthenticated on the next request. Why?
options: The context must be saved explicitly with a SecurityContextRepository
The session cookie name changed to JSESSION
SecurityContextHolder is read-only in Spring Security 6
Custom endpoints must return a JWT
explanation: Spring Security 6 uses SecurityContextHolderFilter, which no longer saves the context automatically.

question: A public method calls a @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") method on this in the same bean. What happens?
options: The check runs as usual
No authorization check occurs because the call bypasses the proxy
Startup fails due to self-invocation
The check runs twice
explanation: Method security uses proxies, and internal calls never pass through them.

question: What does spring.profiles.group.prod=proddb,prodmq do?
options: It creates a prod profile only when proddb and prodmq are both active
It merges the three profiles' files into one file at build time
Activating prod also activates proddb and prodmq
It disables proddb and prodmq when prod is active
explanation: Profile groups let one logical profile expand into several more specific profiles.

question: What happens if spring.profiles.active is set inside application-dev.properties?
options: dev activates the listed profiles recursively
The value is silently ignored
It replaces the profiles from the command line
Startup fails, because it is not allowed in profile-specific documents
explanation: Since Boot 2.4, using spring.profiles.active in a profile-specific document raises an InvalidConfigDataPropertyException.

question: How can one application.properties file contain settings that apply only to the prod profile?
options: Separate documents with #--- and set spring.config.activate.on-profile=prod
Prefix keys with prod. inside the file
Wrap them in a [prod] section header
Use spring.profiles=prod above the keys
explanation: Multi-document properties files use #--- separators, and on-profile activates a document conditionally.

question: dev is active. Which wins: application-dev.properties packaged in the jar, or application.properties in ./config next to the jar?
options: The packaged application-dev.properties
The external ./config/application.properties
Whichever file was modified most recently
Neither; Boot fails because of the conflict
explanation: Boot ranks files outside the jar above packaged ones, including packaged profile-specific files.

question: Why can adding different @MockitoBean declarations across test classes slow a test suite?
options: Mockito must recompile classes for each mock
Mocks disable parallel test execution
Each unique mock set changes the context cache key, forcing new contexts
Mocks force a full Maven rebuild
explanation: Spring's test context cache reuses a context only when configuration, including bean overrides, is identical.

question: A @SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT) test is @Transactional and calls the API via TestRestTemplate. Why are the inserted rows not rolled back?
options: RANDOM_PORT disables all transactions
TestRestTemplate commits the test transaction
Rollback only works with JUnit 4
The server handles the request in a different thread and transaction
explanation: Test-managed rollback applies to the test thread's transaction, not to transactions in server threads.

question: How do you make @DataJpaTest use the real database configured in your properties instead of an embedded one?
options: Add @AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = Replace.NONE)
Add @Transactional(propagation = NEVER)
Set spring.jpa.show-sql=true
Use @SpringBootTest alongside it
explanation: By default @DataJpaTest replaces any DataSource with an embedded one; Replace.NONE keeps yours.

question: Why does @WebMvcTest(UserController.class) fail with NoSuchBeanDefinitionException for UserService?
options: UserService must be annotated with @RestController
The slice does not load @Service beans, so the dependency must be mocked
MockMvc requires services to be static
@WebMvcTest forbids constructor injection
explanation: Provide UserService with @MockitoBean (or @MockBean in older versions) so the controller can be created.

question: In Spring Boot 3, which project replaces Spring Cloud Sleuth for distributed tracing?
options: Spring Cloud Zipkin Starter
OpenCensus Spring
Micrometer Tracing
Actuator Trace Endpoint
explanation: Sleuth's core moved into Micrometer Tracing, built on the Micrometer Observation API.

question: What is the default of management.endpoint.health.show-details?
options: always
when-authorized
on-error
never
explanation: By default only the aggregate status is shown, without component details.

question: What effect does setting management.server.port=9091 have?
options: Actuator endpoints are served on a separate port from the application
The app moves to port 9091 and actuator stays on 8080
All endpoints are disabled except health
Metrics are pushed to a server on port 9091
explanation: A separate management port lets you keep operational endpoints off the public network.

question: In Spring Boot 3, how does /actuator/env show property values by default?
options: Values are shown in plain text
All values are masked
Only passwords are masked
Values are hidden only in the prod profile
explanation: Boot 3 changed show-values to never by default, so values are masked unless configured otherwise.

question: A public method in OrderService calls this.placeOrder(), which is @Transactional. No transaction is active beforehand. What happens?
options: A new transaction starts as normal
Startup fails because of self-invocation
placeOrder runs without a transaction because the call bypasses the proxy
Spring starts a nested transaction
explanation: Self-invocation goes straight to the target object; use a separate bean, self-injection or AspectJ mode.

question: An outer REQUIRED method catches a RuntimeException thrown by an inner REQUIRED method in another bean. What happens at commit?
options: The outer transaction commits normally
Only the inner method's changes are rolled back
The inner method is retried automatically
UnexpectedRollbackException, since the shared transaction was marked rollback-only
explanation: Both methods share one physical transaction, and the inner interceptor marked it rollback-only.

question: How does Propagation.NESTED differ from REQUIRES_NEW?
options: NESTED uses a savepoint in the same physical transaction, REQUIRES_NEW starts a separate one
NESTED creates a new database connection, REQUIRES_NEW does not
NESTED ignores rollback, REQUIRES_NEW does not
They are identical aliases
explanation: Rolling back a nested scope returns to the savepoint, but an outer rollback also undoes the nested work.

question: What is the default phase of a @TransactionalEventListener?
options: BEFORE_COMMIT
AFTER_COMMIT
AFTER_ROLLBACK
AFTER_COMPLETION
explanation: The listener runs only after the publishing transaction commits successfully, unless another phase is set.

question: Why can't you switch @Profile-based beans at runtime in a Spring Boot GraalVM native image?
options: Native images cannot read environment variables
Profiles are only supported in WAR deployments
AOT processing fixes the bean definitions at build time
GraalVM strips all annotations
explanation: Native images assume a closed world, so profiles and conditions are evaluated during the AOT build.

question: In an executable Spring Boot jar, what does the manifest's Main-Class point to?
options: Your @SpringBootApplication class directly
org.apache.catalina.startup.Bootstrap
java.lang.ClassLoader
Spring Boot's JarLauncher, with Start-Class naming your application class
explanation: The launcher sets up a class loader for the nested jars and then invokes Start-Class.

question: Why does spring-boot-devtools not affect an app started with java -jar from a packaged jar?
options: Devtools turns itself off when the app runs as a fully packaged application
Maven deletes devtools during packaging
Devtools needs the prod profile
java -jar ignores every optional dependency
explanation: Devtools treats a packaged launch as production and disables itself; repackage also excludes it by default.

question: With spring-boot-starter-parent, how do you usually override the managed version of Jackson?
options: Edit the starter jar's MANIFEST.MF
Set the jackson-bom.version property in the pom
Add @JacksonVersion to the main class
Delete the dependencyManagement section
explanation: The parent manages versions through properties, so redefining one changes the version used.
